The universal claim in config.py:118-126 ('when it is >= similarity_threshold (the default) the band is empty and injection behaves exactly as before') and the matching enhancer docstring in default.py:51-56 ('...the band is empty and injection is unchanged') hold only for the literal default values (0.7/0.7); they are false for other equal (or context_floor > strict) configurations. Pre-change code (git show af396aa:src/sqllens/agent/core/enhancer/default.py, lines ~74-79) called `self.agent_memory.search_text_memories(query=user_message, context=context, limit=5)` with NO similarity_threshold argument at all, so it always used the hard-coded default of 0.7 defined on both the ABC (src/sqllens/agent/capabilities/agent_memory/base.py:60-69, default 0.7) and the concrete ChromaDB implementation (src/sqllens/agent/integrations/chromadb/agent_memory.py:392-398, default 0.7) -- completely independent of `cfg.memory.similarity_threshold`. Post-change code (src/sqllens/agent/core/enhancer/default.py:96-112) computes `text_search_floor = min(context_floor, strict)` and passes it explicitly: `similarity_threshold=text_search_floor`. Falsifying case: set similarity_threshold=0.5 and context_similarity_threshold=0.5 (equal, non-default, matching the hint's '0.5/0.5' construction). band_enabled = (0.5 < 0.5) = False, so band_pairs stays empty and search_similar_usage is never called -- that half of the claim holds. But text_search_floor = min(0.5, 0.5) = 0.5, which is passed to search_text_memories, replacing the pre-change hard-coded 0.7. This is strictly more permissive than before (0.5 < 0.7), so text memories scoring in [0.5, 0.7) that were NEVER injected pre-change are now injected post-change even though the band is 'empty' and band_enabled is False. Injection is therefore NOT 'exactly as before' / 'unchanged' whenever similarity_threshold != 0.7, contradicting the universal-sounding docstring wording in both files. This is exactly the failure mode the verify_hint flagged (pre-change hard-coded 0.7 floor vs. the new similarity_threshold-derived floor). The property only holds in the special case similarity_threshold == 0.7 (which happens to be the field's own default), not for the general '>=' condition as stated.
